answer_1.quote: We introduce a new NLP task: predicting identity fusion from natural language, and evaluate its utility on a downstream task-violence risk prediction.
tasks: Other:predicting identity fusion from natural language
answer_1.outputs: The outputs include predicted identity fusion levels (low, medium, high) and violence risk classification (Violent Self-Sacrificial, Ideologically Extreme, Moderate).

answer_2.quote: CLIFS raised classification performance 6-154% over baselines and surpassed human annotation by 11-22%. In fine-grained identity fusion estimation, it cut error rates 25% and boosted monotonic correlation by 10% versus human annotations...

answer_3.quote: We use OpenAI's gpt-4o model, and adapt a prompt structure from prior work that improved text classification performance.

answer_4.quote: We compare our model performance against human annotations on 97 college-target samples.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators were asked to classify texts into low, medium, or high identity fusion based on the Verbal Identity Fusion Scale (VIFS) and definitions derived from CIFT.
